observations: Photo 0 shows the retail packaging for a Mercury Maverick 1050 UPS.
The box is stacked on top of other electronics boxes, specifically Blue Gate branded UPS boxes.
The actual UPS unit is not visible in the photo; only the cardboard box is shown.
The box appears to be in a retail or warehouse environment.

claims.claim: UPS provides a reliable power back up
claims.evidence: The photo only shows the box; the internal battery health and circuit functionality cannot be confirmed remotely.

claims.claim: enables you save your work the moment there is power [cut]
claims.evidence: This is a general product description and requires a load test to verify for this specific unit.

risks.risk: The internal lead-acid battery may be depleted, sulfated, or dead due to age or storage conditions.
risks.proof: A video of the UPS powering a significant load (e.g., a desktop PC or a large lamp) for several minutes while unplugged from the wall.
risks.if_unproven: as having a dead battery requiring immediate replacement

risks.risk: The box may be empty, contain a different model, or contain a physically damaged unit.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the actual UPS unit from all sides, out of the packaging.
risks.if_unproven: as a damaged or incomplete unit

risks.risk: Internal electronic failure or blown inverter components.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit successfully passing its self-test upon being switched on.

proof_requests: Photos of the actual UPS unit outside of the box to verify condition and model.
A video showing the unit turned on and supporting a load while the power cord is disconnected.
A photo of the manufacturer's sticker on the back of the actual unit showing the serial number and date of manufacture.
response.reason: The brand and model are clearly identified from the retail packaging. It is priced at the worst-case scenario (non-functional with a dead battery) because the actual device is not shown and its condition is unverified.
